articles.title: 삼성 파운드리, 美클라로스와 맞손…AI 데이터센터용 전력반도체 양산
articles.body:
Samsung Electronics' Foundry Division has entered a strategic manufacturing partnership with American power management startup Claros to mass-produce next-generation power semiconductors for AI data centers.

Claros announced on June 16 (local time) that it has agreed to establish large-scale production of its flagship "Integrated Voltage Regulator (IVR)" product using Samsung Foundry's process technology. This collaboration addresses a critical challenge facing global hyperscalers: data center power consumption.

The IVR precisely controls data center power immediately before the processor stage. In traditional 800VDC data center environments, power transmission incurs significant losses. By applying this technology, power can be regulated directly millimeters from the processor unit, reducing energy loss by up to 30%.

Samsung will provide its 14-nanometer FinFET advanced process line located in the United States to manufacture Claros' next-generation IVR products.

Margaret Han, Vice President of Samsung Electronics' U.S. Foundry Division, stated: "Processor-level power delivery represents a key challenge for current AI infrastructure," emphasizing expectations that this technology will expand beyond data centers into industrial and automotive semiconductor sectors.

Claros, which recently secured $30 million in seed funding, aims to accelerate resolution of power infrastructure bottlenecks in the AI accelerator market.

articles.title: "데이터는 21세기 원유"…조현준, AI 데이터센터 승부수
articles.body:
Hyosung Group Chairman Cho Hyun-jun has launched a data center venture that marks the company's pivot toward AI and cloud infrastructure. The joint venture between Hyosung and Singapore-based ST Telemetry Global Data Center (STT GDC) opened "STT Seoul 1" in the Gasan Digital Complex in Geumcheon-gu, Seoul.

The facility operates as a hyperscale data center with 30MW IT capacity, designed to handle power-intensive operations like large-scale cloud services and AI computing. Its urban location near major business districts offers customers reduced latency and improved service accessibility compared to data centers typically built outside Seoul.

The infrastructure combines Hyosung Heavy Industries' power equipment technology with STT GDC's data center design and operations expertise. The facility achieved Tier 3 TCDD certification from the Uptime Institute.

Cho emphasized that "data will become the crude oil of the 21st century," noting the facility reflects his vision of AI competitiveness becoming national competitiveness. He directed the group to develop data center operations as a core growth engine.

Hyosung plans to leverage its three-decade IT operations experience alongside its power systems and construction capabilities. Hyosung Heavy Industries will supply power equipment and handle construction, while Hyosung ITX will manage traffic, security, and operational systems using cloud expertise gained over decades.

The company intends to expand data center operations to meet growing domestic AI and cloud demand, establishing long-term revenue streams by connecting traditional power equipment business with data center construction, operations, and IT services.

articles.title: 구글, '안드로이드 17' 출시…"AI로 멀티태스킹 강화"
articles.body:
구글이 최신 AI 모델을 앞세워 기기 내 인공지능 기능을 확대했다. 16일(현지시간) 구글은 '안드로이드 17' 운영체제와 스마트워치용 '웨어 OS 7'을 공식 출시했으며, 이번 업데이트는 구글 '픽셀' 기기에 먼저 적용된다.

픽셀 드롭에는 음악 생성 모델 '리리아 3'와 멀티모달 모델 '제미나이 옴니'가 포함됐다. 제미나이 옴니는 대화 중 동영상 편집을 지원하며, 리리아 3는 텍스트 프롬프트나 이미지를 활용해 음악 트랙 생성을 돕는다.

픽셀 10a에는 오디오LM 기반 음성 번역 기능도 개선되어 제공된다. 안드로이드 17의 새로운 사용자 인터페이스인 '버블 바'는 화면 하단에 최근 앱을 버블 형태로 정리하여 빠른 접근을 가능하게 한다.

추가 기능으로는 셀피 카메라와 휴대전화 화면을 동시에 녹화하는 화면 녹화 기능, 긴급 감지 기능, 실시간 위협 탐지 강화 등이 포함됐다. 올여름에는 웨어 OS에 더 많은 제미나이 인텔리전스 기능이 도입될 예정이다.

articles.title: AI 칩 임대비용도 원유처럼 선물시장서 거래 추진
articles.body:
AI computing power is moving toward commoditized futures trading. Silicon Data, an AI market research firm, is collaborating with the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) to launch futures contracts based on data center computing capacity needed for AI model training and operation.

The initiative standardizes rental fees for high-performance GPUs like Nvidia's H100 chip, enabling them to trade on futures markets similarly to crude oil, precious metals, and agricultural products.

Silicon Data has developed a GPU price index tracking hourly rental costs across various AI chips. As data center infrastructure demand surges, GPU rental volatility has increased significantly. Both data center users and providers seek to hedge against future price uncertainty.

These AI computing power futures contracts currently undergo regulatory review by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). ETF operators including ProShares and Grayscale have already submitted ETF product proposals based on Silicon Data's proposed futures contracts.

According to CNBC, "This movement suggests some investors increasingly view AI computing not merely as a tech cost item but as a potentially tradable asset class." CME Group and Silicon Data announced their partnership on May 12, 2026, with the futures contracts pending regulatory review. Major financial institutions Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan are also exploring strategies centered around GPU rental price futures to hedge against potential oversupply risks while enabling clients to lock in costs.

articles.title: 수출입은행, 두산 태국 AI 반도체 소재 거점에 1억1000만달러 지원
articles.body:
The Korea Export-Import Bank is providing $110 million to support Doosan Group's establishment of a high-performance copper clad laminate (CCL) production facility in Thailand, in response to the global AI semiconductor supply chain reorganization.

This funding initiative aligns with global IT enterprises' supply chain shifts to help Korean companies secure market leadership. Doosan plans to secure a production base in Thailand's Arayal Industrial Complex as AI semiconductor supply chains expand into Southeast Asia, with construction beginning within the year.

The core materials—copper clad laminates—are experiencing surging demand due to expanded global AI data center investments.

The Export-Import Bank intends to broaden financial support across the entire AI value chain, starting with semiconductor materials and extending to physical AI and energy infrastructure. The bank will support export-import financing and overseas investments for Doosan Tesna (semiconductor back-end processing) and Doosan Robotics, while discussing financial support with Doosan Enerbility (small modular reactors).

This represents the first outcome of an April business agreement between the Export-Import Bank and Doosan Group. The initiative reflects South Korea's strategic push to secure AI semiconductor supply chains amid global competition between the U.S., China, and other major economies.

articles.title: [6월16일] 나델라가 경고한 'AI 공동화'…"AI는 소수 모델이 아닌 모든 기업의 문제"
articles.body:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warned against "AI hollowing out" of industries, arguing that concentration of value in a few AI models poses systemic risks similar to 20th-century outsourcing.

Nadella stated: "A frontier without an ecosystem is not stable" and expressed concern that "all value concentrated in a few models" would be "politically and economically untenable."

He drew parallels to manufacturing offshoring, where short-term productivity gains preceded long-term erosion of industrial ecosystems. Similarly, companies over-reliant on external AI models risk losing accumulated expertise and decision-making capabilities.

Nadella emphasized "cognitive loops"—iterative human-AI interactions—as the real competitive advantage. Companies should build "token capital" from their business processes: data, documents, prompts, and domain knowledge processed by AI systems.

The key distinction: enterprises must retain intellectual property while improving agent-based systems over time, avoiding vendor lock-in. This requires architectural approaches enabling model portability without sacrificing specialized knowledge.

He argued the future competition shifts from "model development" by a few AI firms to "learning competitions" among enterprises using AI, making human expertise and organizational learning critical again. This positions AI as a broadly distributed enterprise tool rather than a product controlled by a small number of frontier model providers.

articles.title: 메타 내부 회의서 갈등 폭발… '가혹한 환경'
articles.body:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg acknowledged in an internal memo dated June 12, 2026, that the company had made mistakes while restructuring its workforce around artificial intelligence. Around 8,000 employees were laid off in May, while approximately 7,000 others were transferred to AI-related initiatives. Together, the layoffs and transfers affected nearly one-fifth of Meta's workforce.

Several employees reportedly described themselves as "draftees" because they had little choice over their transfer, with assignments including developing coding problems, puzzles, and other material used to train and evaluate AI models. Some employees described the environment as a "gulag" and "soul-crushing."

Zuckerberg reiterated that Meta does not expect further company-wide layoffs in 2026. Meta is also introducing measures to address employee morale and improve collaboration, including higher budgets for team events and offsites, as well as a company-wide hackathon planned for July to accelerate work on the company's latest AI models.

The restructuring reflects a broader industry trend where hyperscalers are reorganizing human capital around AI development priorities. Meta's aggressive AI workforce pivot has generated significant internal friction, with employees questioning the rapid pace of change and limited individual agency in the reassignment process. The company plans to spend up to $135 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026.

articles.title: HPE Discover 2026 Keynote Coverage
articles.body:
Patrick Kennedy attended HPE Discover 2026 in Las Vegas to cover CEO Antonio Neri's keynote presentation. The event showcased HPE's integration of Juniper Networks and focused heavily on networking and AI infrastructure announcements.

The keynote opened with emphasis on HPE's self-driving network capabilities rather than compute, signaling a strategic messaging shift. Kennedy noted this differed from competing vendors' approaches, observing that "this felt like a networking company doing AI compute, versus a compute company selling networking."

Key Product Announcements:

HPE introduced several networking solutions optimized for AI workloads:
- QFS5252 Scale-up Switch: A liquid-cooled switch supporting UALink over Ethernet and SONiC operations, featuring dual Broadcom Tomahawk 6 architecture
- QFX5250 Scale-out Switch: Delivering 102.5Tbps capacity with liquid cooling for distributed deployments
- PTX Routing Family: Supporting 800Gbps routing with ZR/ZR+ coherent optics for data center interconnection
- SRX4700 Firewall: A quantum-safe 1.4Tbps firewall in 1U form factor
- MX301 Router: Providing 1.6Tbps full-duplex capacity for inference edge deployments
- QFX5140 Inference Switch: A 16Tbps switch optimized for inference workloads

AI and Enterprise Solutions:

HPE announced the AMD Helios AI rack solution integrated with Juniper networking components. The company detailed three AI deployment models: HPE Private Cloud AI for enterprises, HPE AI Factory at Scale for neoclouds and hyperscalers, and HPE AI Factory Sovereign for government and defense sectors.

The Private Cloud AI platform incorporates NVIDIA integration, real-time data enrichment, and native MCP (Model Context Protocol) capabilities through the HPE Alletra Storage MP X10000 file and object storage system.

Agentic AI Capabilities:

HPE emphasized its Agentic Enterprise initiatives, including agent governance, registration, and security frameworks. The company announced support for NVIDIA OpenShell and NemoClaw standards for AI agent interoperability.

HPE AI Factory With NVIDIA Expands: HPE Private Cloud AI adds HPE ProLiant Compute DL394 Gen12 with NVIDIA Vera CPU as a compute-optimized foundation for agentic AI. NVIDIA Agent Toolkit software — including NVIDIA Nemotron open models, NVIDIA NemoClaw, and the NVIDIA OpenShell secure runtime — provide an agent operating system that efficiently reasons, with policy enforcement and behavioral monitoring.

Additional Announcements:

Other highlighted topics included HPE ProLiant Gen12 compute systems, HPE Nonstop updates with Intel Xeon 6, HPE CloudOps bringing VMware Morpheus to broader ecosystems, cyber resilience features, and expanded GreenLake cloud services with integrated AIOps capabilities. The event was HPE's first major Discover since its $14 billion acquisition of Juniper Networks.

articles.title: LG이노텍 베트남 FC-BGA 라인 증설 고객사와 협의 중
articles.body:
LG Innotek announced plans to invest approximately 1 trillion won in Vietnam's Hai Phong to expand semiconductor substrate production. The company is in active discussions with customers regarding a second phase of investment focused on FC-BGA (flip-chip ball grid array) line expansion for AI server applications.

According to Jo Ji-tae, head of the Package Solution Business Division, the company is "in concrete discussions with multiple customers on investment methods" and expects to announce the scale "soon."

The first investment phase targets PS (Package Substrate) business expansion, including RF-SiP and FC-CSP products. The second phase would establish dedicated FC-BGA substrate production facilities, as these require specialized equipment using ABF (Ajinomoto Build-up Film) instead of standard BT resin.

Domestically, LG Innotek is considering additional FC-BGA capacity expansion at its Gumi facility in Gyeongbuk, positioning both locations as major production hubs.

The company targets 1 trillion won in FC-BGA revenues by 2030, representing one-third of its 3 trillion won Package Solution business goal. Network AI server substrates are planned for mass production in H2 2026, with learning and inference substrates targeting 2027.

The expansion responds to new CPU-based semiconductor ecosystems emerging among U.S. and Taiwanese customers developing custom ASIC supply chains. LG Innotek is positioning itself as a diversified substrate supplier beyond GPU-focused networks, meeting demand from hyperscalers and AI server manufacturers requiring high-density FC-BGA packages for next-generation AI inference and training processors.

articles.title: 애플, 2028년 아이폰에 1.4nm A22 Pro 칩…인텔 파운드리 일부 위탁
articles.body:
Apple plans to equip its 2028 flagship iPhone with a 1.4-nanometer A22 Pro chip, according to Bloomberg. While Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) will primarily handle production, Apple is exploring options to assign some volume to Intel.

The current iPhone 17 series uses TSMC's third-generation 3-nanometer process (N3P). The upcoming iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and foldable iPhone launching this fall are expected to feature next-generation 2-nanometer chips. The 2-nanometer process will continue for 2027 products, with a planned transition to 1.4-nanometer for certain 2028 models.

TSMC's A14 process (1.4-nanometer class) is projected to deliver up to 15% improved performance compared to 2-nanometer, while reducing power consumption by up to 30% at equivalent performance levels.

"As processes become more advanced, production costs increase significantly and yield assurance becomes challenging," the report notes. TSMC's capacity is further constrained by surging artificial intelligence server chip demand.

To mitigate supply chain risks, Apple is diversifying its semiconductor partners. Intel, currently developing its 14A node (1.4-nanometer class) with 2028 mass production goals, may manufacture ARM-based chips designed by Apple — a notable shift from Apple's historical reliance on Intel-designed processors for Mac products.

This development coincides with Intel's announcement at the 2026 VLSI Symposium that its 18A-P process has entered risk production, demonstrating the company's progress in advanced semiconductor manufacturing. A potential Apple deal would validate Intel Foundry's external customer strategy.

articles.title: AI안전연구소-오픈AI, 'AI 안전 협력 강화' MOU 체결
articles.body:
The South Korean government has expanded its cooperation with OpenAI to strengthen artificial intelligence safety verification for cutting-edge models.

The Ministry of Science and ICT announced that the AI Safety Research Institute signed a memorandum of understanding with OpenAI on June 17 at ETRI's Seoul office to enhance safety collaboration in high-risk AI domains.

This agreement builds upon a previous memorandum between the ministry and OpenAI from October of the previous year, extending cooperation specifically to AI safety. The initiative emerged from discussions during two separate meetings between ministry officials and OpenAI executives.

The AI Safety Research Institute and OpenAI will share knowledge regarding safety assessment methodologies, benchmarks, and best practices across high-risk sectors. They will also exchange technical information for developing evaluation systems that reflect Korean language and societal context.

As high-performance and autonomous agent AI systems expand into critical areas including finance, healthcare, security, and public services, the importance of pre-deployment safety assessments has increased substantially. Evaluation frameworks must now examine not only model performance but also potential malfunctions, societal biases, and misuse risks.

South Korea is the fourth country — following the United States, United Kingdom, and Japan — where OpenAI has established such a partnership with a national AI safety research institute.

The two organizations plan to continue collaborating on establishing internationally applicable AI safety evaluation standards, with specific cooperation projects and timelines to be finalized through subsequent technical discussions.

articles.title: AI 인프라 플랫폼 텐, 과기부 '글로벌 ICT 미래 유니콘' 선정…리벨리온도 포함
articles.body:
AI infrastructure platform company Ten (CEO Oh Se-jin) has been selected as a supporting company for the "2026 Global ICT Future Unicorn Development Project (ICT GROWTH)" organized by the Ministry of Science and ICT and the National IT Industry Promotion Agency (NIPA).

This national initiative aims to discover and nurture ICT companies into unicorn enterprises. Fifteen companies, including Ten and Rebellion, were selected based on evaluations of technological excellence, market expansion potential, and investment achievements.

Through this selection, Ten will receive growth support including global market entry programs, investment and financing connections, and startup/venture support linkages. The company plans to expand operations in the United States and Singapore through global expansion initiatives.

Ten developed "AIPub," an AI infrastructure platform based on GPU optimization and AI workload orchestration technology. The platform can subdivide GPU resources into units of up to 100 and allocate them according to AI workloads, with goals to enhance operational efficiency through GPU monitoring, scheduling, autoscaling, and usage-based analysis (FinOps) capabilities.

CEO Oh emphasized that the selection "recognizes Ten's AI infrastructure optimization technology and global growth potential," adding the company will "continuously improve GPU optimization and workload orchestration technologies."

Rebellions, the domestic AI accelerator startup also selected in this cohort, has been expanding its ATOM NPU ecosystem following its $400 million pre-IPO round and a 2.3 trillion won valuation. The company's NPU is already deployed in KT Cloud's public-sector cloud services and recently announced renewed Middle East expansion efforts.

articles.title: Anthropic's latest feud with the Trump admin may actually help it, sales data suggests
articles.body:
Anthropic is experiencing remarkable momentum despite regulatory friction. The company surpassed OpenAI in business spending market share for the first time in May, raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation, and filed confidential IPO paperwork while reporting its first profitable quarter.

However, the Trump administration sent a letter Friday demanding Anthropic ban non-Americans — including its own employees — from accessing its advanced models: the limited-release Mythos 5 and publicly available Fable 5. This forced the company to withdraw its latest model entirely.

Despite this government pressure, business adoption continues accelerating. According to Ramp data from over 70,000 companies, Anthropic captured 41% of AI subscription spending in May, compared to OpenAI's 39.5%. Ramp's lead economist notes: "If anything, it'll probably boost them. Anthropic's best month on record...was the month that the Department of Defense labeled them a supply-chain risk."

Businesses primarily use Claude Opus models and the company's Claude Code tool for AI-powered development work. While exact financial impact from the model withdrawal remains unclear, available models show stronger business popularity than ever.

The article also notes that Claude has "gained a strong reputation for productivity use cases" and approaches ChatGPT's retention rates. Gemini benefits from integration with Google's ecosystem, capturing 27.7% market share with 662 million users.

Industry-wide metrics show maturation. H1 2026 projects 2.3 billion AI app downloads and $4.2 billion spending, compared to $1.83 billion in H1 2025. Claude demonstrates strongest monetization, with 13% of users paying for subscriptions — "a conversion rate that leads the field."

articles.title: Intel Foundry Details Process Milestones and Future Innovation at VLSI Symposium — Intel 18A-P Enters Risk Production
articles.body:
Intel Foundry announced progress on its Intel 18A-P process node at the 2026 VLSI Symposium. Intel 18A-P, described as "the first performance enhancement in the Intel 18A family," has entered risk production, meeting previously communicated timelines.

Performance Improvements:
Intel 18A-P delivers 9% higher performance at iso-power or 18% lower power at iso-performance compared to Intel 18A, alongside enhanced thermal characteristics and expanded design flexibility. Specific improvements include:
- Power Boost technology: a dual contact, low resistance transistor option enabling increased drive current and greater frequency at matched capacitance
- 20-40% improved thermal resistance through both materials and design innovations
- 10-30% improved via resistance using geometric and materials optimizations
- Full design rule compatibility with Intel 18A, allowing straightforward IP reuse
- Two cell heights (180nm and 160nm) with 50nm contacted poly pitch
- New fifth logic threshold voltage option for balancing speed and power

Backside Power Delivery Results: Intel demonstrated 11% routed area reduction and 10x dynamic voltage droop reduction, enabling up to 6% frequency uplift or greater than 15% dynamic power reduction.

Future Research: Intel presented work on complementary FET (CFET) inverters achieving 45nm contacted poly pitch, gallium nitride plus silicon integration on 300mm wafers for power management, and subtractive ruthenium interconnect technology achieving up to 35% capacitance reduction.

Intel 18A is now ramping in two U.S. fabrication facilities with declining defect density. The node integrates RibbonFET gate-all-around transistors and PowerVia backside power delivery.

Analysts noted that the 18A-P announcement — alongside reports of Apple exploring Intel Foundry for 1.4nm production — marks a potential inflection point for Intel's external foundry business, which has struggled to win major customers against TSMC.

articles.title: Tensordyne Converts AI Matrix Math To Logs To Crank Up Inference Oomph
articles.body:
Tensordyne, an AI inference chip startup, has developed the Napier computing engine that converts matrix multiplication operations into logarithmic addition operations, dramatically improving inference performance and efficiency.

The Napier chip features 48 logarithmic cores, vector processing units, and RISC-V processors, implementing 138 billion transistors in a 3-nanometer process. It consumes only 300 watts compared to 1,200 watts for Nvidia's Blackwell B300 GPU.

Founders RK Anand (Chief Product Officer) and Gilles Backhus (VP of AI) previously collaborated at Kumu Networks on full-duplex wireless technology. The company, which raised $176 million across three funding rounds, pivoted from automotive AI to datacenter inference around 2022. Founded in 2017 as Recogni, the startup rebranded to Tensordyne last year.

Performance Claims:
A single rack of 288 Napier devices delivers 608 petaflops at FP8 precision while consuming 120 kilowatts and supporting air cooling. Tensordyne claims comparable token throughput to GPU systems using one-sixth the rack space and 30% less power.

The company expects more than $200 million in orders for its system, with over a dozen letters of intent from companies planning to evaluate beta systems. AI infrastructure providers Cirrascale and BlueSky Compute have expressed interest.

Technical approach: Traditional matrix multiplication requires multiplying pairs of numbers and summing results — a compute-intensive process. Tensordyne's approach converts numbers to their logarithmic equivalents, allowing multiplications to become additions, which are less compute-intensive. The downside is potential precision loss, which the company claims to handle through architectural innovations.

The chip is produced by TSMC and was developed in partnership with Broadcom and HPE-owned Juniper Networks.

Timeline: Cloud access expected by end of 2026; customer shipments begin Q1 2027.

articles.title: VAST Data and the evolving neoclouds
articles.body:
VAST Data dominates neocloud storage, cementing its position with a 600 PB capacity deployment at Australia's Sharon AI. The neoclouds — emerging competitors to traditional hyperscalers — are expanding beyond GPU-intensive AI services into managed service provider (MSP) offerings and sovereign datacenters.

Neoclouds originated from cryptocurrency mining operations that pivoted to GPU-based cloud services after the 2018 crypto crash. The ChatGPT launch in late 2022 catalyzed explosive growth in AI model training demand. Neocloud revenues reached $23-25 billion in 2025, more than triple their 2024 figures, with market leader CoreWeave reporting $5.13 billion in 2025 revenues — surpassing AWS's $15 billion AI revenue run rate.

VAST Data CTO Alon Horev explains that neoclouds prioritize all-flash storage to prevent GPU idle time: "We're getting two to one data reduction" through efficient flash utilization. Unlike traditional tiered architectures, keeping data on flash ensures continuous GPU availability, which proves economically critical given hardware costs.

Neoclouds are transitioning from dedicated customer environments toward multi-tenant, hyperscaler-like infrastructure models. This shift enables flexible consumption-based pricing — "pay per gig" rather than three-year prepaid commitments — and improves margins.

Traditional MSPs and telecom providers are exploring neocloud transitions, though significant expertise gaps remain. AI inferencing demands differ substantially from virtual machine services, requiring knowledge of specialized networking (InfiniBand, Spectrum X), liquid cooling, and containerization technologies.

VAST assists neoclouds transitioning toward enterprise customers by implementing security features essential for inference workloads: FIPS compliance, multi-tenancy isolation, encryption protocols, and external key manager support.

The convergence creates expansion opportunities: neoclouds move toward MSP-type services while MSPs gradually adopt AI capabilities. The analysis suggests the neocloud sector will increasingly resemble traditional hyperscalers over the next three to five years.
